_comment_family: Special Elite ships as a single style - one file, one cut, no
siblings in fonts/ and none at the foundry either - so name ID 1 is
both the family and the only thing that can answer to it. It is
declared as the file's own 'Special Elite' for garet-book's reason:
the honest name is the one the file states, and there is no second
weight here for a bare family name to be confused with.
That is the whole difference between this pack and the two Telegraf
ones, which declare a full name because two files in this folder
carry one family between them. Nothing of the kind is possible with
a family of one. The day a second cut of it appears this pack has to
be revisited - which is the same day telegraf-ultralight's note
describes, arriving from the other direction.
Weight 400, which is the file's own usWeightClass. The face LOOKS
heavier than a 400 because its letters are struck rather than drawn
- ink spreads at the edges of every stem - and that is a property of
the outlines and not of the weight axis. Asking for 700 here would
invite a browser to synthesise a bold on top of a face that is
already carrying its own ink.
One thing to know before measuring anything against this file: its
OS/2 sCapHeight and sxHeight are wrong, by a consistent factor of
about 1.87 - the table says 713 units of cap where the 'H' actually
inks 1412. Nothing here reads them (the renderer measures an 'H'
through the canvas, see capBand in js/text.js), so it costs the app
nothing; it is written down because somebody checking this face's
size against its metrics table will otherwise be checking it against
a number the drawing does not use.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the PostScript name and is also what the installer
registers the face under; the second is the Windows full name; the
'Special Elite' on its own is present here, where every other pack in
this folder deliberately leaves the bare family out. Those families
have other cuts that answer to the family name, and a Light handed
back in place of a Bold is a silent wrong face. This family has one
cut, so the family name and this file name the same thing and there
is nothing for it to be confused with.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied, and here the choice
is narrow: what makes this face this face is that it is a TYPEWRITER,
and a fallback that is not one loses the only thing the channel
So Courier New, which is on every Windows there is and is the one
typewriter face that can be relied on, with Consolas behind it for
the same reason at a slightly better fitted weight. Both are
monospaced where this face is proportional, so the metrics are wrong
in a way a caption will show - that is what a fallback IS here, and
fontguard still fails the channel over a missing file rather than
letting one of them be drawn quietly.
Impact and Arial Black, which most of this folder falls back through,
are absent for american-typewriter-itc-pro-bold's reason: they are
heavy display grotesques, and falling back from a struck typewriter
to one of them would make the one thing that survives a missing file
the furthest possible thing from it.
